description: We are Team Xisco, a multidisciplinary team passionate about software engineering, AI, data science, and geospatial technology. We aim to use innovation and NASA data to develop practical solutions to real-world challenges, particularly in agriculture and climate adaptation. Our team welcomes creative, committed members skilled in programming, GIS, remote sensing, agriculture, UI/UX, and research. Let's build something impactful!
summary:
SeasonLens is a smart, multilingual agricultural decision-support platform that helps farmers make informed, climate-aware farming decisions using NASA Earth observation data and agricultural information.

Farmers worldwide face increasing challenges from unpredictable rainfall, changing temperatures, soil variability, and shifting growing seasons, which can lead to poor planting decisions, crop losses, and reduced yields. SeasonLens addresses these challenges by transforming complex environmental and agricultural data into practical, location-specific farming recommendations.

The platform integrates NASA satellite-derived data, including rainfall, land surface temperature, and vegetation observations, with soil information and documented crop requirements. It analyzes these factors to identify suitable planting periods, assess crop-growing conditions, and provide crop-specific recommendations and risk alerts.

By translating scientific satellite observations into accessible, actionable guidance, SeasonLens bridges the gap between space technology and everyday farming. Our goal is to empower farmers across different regions, regardless of their technological or educational backgrounds, to adapt to changing environmental conditions, reduce climate-related risks, improve agricultural productivity, and strengthen global food security.
details:
Project Functionality

SeasonLens is a web app that compares a farm's current season with its historical norm. The farmer picks a location and crop. SeasonLens then shows rainfall, temperature and vegetation health against past seasons, and flags planting windows and crop stress.

Problem Addressed

Climate variability is shifting rainfall patterns and growing seasons. Traditional planting calendars are becoming unreliable, and many farmers lack accessible, data-driven tools to adapt.

Solution

SeasonLens turns satellite data into plain-language guidance: when to plant, when to irrigate, and when crops are under stress. Farmers get a clear recommendation instead of raw data.

NASA Integration

Collected: daily temperature, solar radiation and rainfall from NASA POWER, precipitation from GPM IMERG, and vegetation health (NDVI) from MODIS.

Processed: data is fetched by coordinates and date, cleaned, and aggregated by week. Each season is compared with a multi-year baseline to detect anomalies.

Used: results become charts, a season-status indicator and recommendations.

Benefits

Better-timed planting and irrigation, less water and input waste, earlier warning of crop stress, and free access from any browser.

Intended Impact

Greater farm resilience to climate variability, more efficient water use, and less environmental strain from over-irrigation and poorly timed inputs.

[Replace with your actual stack, e.g. JavaScript/React, Python, REST APIs, GitHub, hosting platform.]

Hardware/Software

Standard laptops, a code editor, GitHub for version control, and a cloud hosting platform.

Creativity

Most tools show raw weather data. SeasonLens interprets the whole season against history, so non-experts can act on NASA data without technical knowledge.

Design Considerations

Accessibility: simple language, high-contrast colors, mobile-friendly layout.

Usability: two inputs (location, crop) and one clear result screen.

Local conditions: guidance is tuned to regional rainfall patterns and crop calendars, with light pages for low connectivity.
